o: Skin creases have thinner epidermis and thicker dermis
Bound firmly to underlying fascia.
The panniculus carnosus forms palmaris brevis in man
And dartos, platysma and facial muscles.
Deep fascia passes freely over bone
It is always anchored firmly to periosteum.
Deep fascia has its own nerve supply distinct from the overlying skin
It shares the innervation of the overlying skin.
Only fibrocartilage has a blood supply
The others rely on diffusion.
The epiglottis is elastic cartilage
As is the pinna.
Secondary cartilage is the cartilage of secondary cartilaginous joints
It is a special cartilage of growing membrane bones such as the mandibular head and clavicle.
Menisci of the knee are hyaline cartilage
Fibrocartilage.
Yellow ligaments include the ligamenta flava
And capsular ligaments of the auditory ossicles.
The epiphyseal plate is a primary cartilaginous joint
True. In a primary cartilaginous joint bone meets hyaline cartilage directly, as at the epiphyseal plate; it allows no movement. (Last's)
The pubic symphysis is a primary cartilaginous joint
Secondary (symphysis).
Hilton's law states that a joint's nerve supplies only its capsule
The nerve to a muscle also supplies the joint it moves and the overlying skin.
The parietal layer of serosa develops from somatopleure
Supplied segmentally by spinal nerves.
The visceral layer has no sensory supply
Autonomic only.
The pulmonary veins have valves
They are valveless.
Veins have an internal elastic lamina like arteries
They lack one.
Perineurium joins fibres into fascicles
True. Endoneurium surrounds each fibre, perineurium binds fibres into fascicles and epineurium binds fascicles into the nerve. (Last's)
The phrenic nerve takes its own artery through the mediastinum
The pericardiacophrenic.
Endoneurium binds fascicles into a nerve
That is epineurium.
About 10% of fibres in a muscle nerve are afferent
About 40%.
There are 31 pairs
Anterior roots contain some unmyelinated afferent pain fibres
They double back from the DRG.
Spinal nerves lie in the spinal canal
The roots unite in the intervertebral foramen; no spinal nerves lie in the canal.
The spinal nerve proper is about 1 cm long
1-2 mm at best.
The trochlear and abducent nuclei are the exception to overlapping motor pools
Each supplies a single muscle.
More distal joints are controlled from lower cord segments
True. For each joint further down the limb the spinal centre lies one segment lower (e.g. shoulder C5, elbow C6-7, wrist C6-7, hand C8-T1). (Last's)
Cutaneous nerve lesions cause proprioceptive loss
Cutaneous nerves carry no muscle proprioceptive fibres.
Muscles sharing an action are usually supplied by different segments
The same segments.

questions.s: Nerves and vessels of the body wall (Last's):
o: Where nerve and segmental artery cross, the nerve lies nearer the skin
True. Where the spinal nerve and segmental artery cross, the nerve is always the more superficial. (Last's)
The sympathetic trunk lies within the circle of the segmental artery
True. The sympathetic trunk lies vertically within the circle made by each segmental artery. (Last's)
Posterior rami supply limb muscles
Never.
The collateral intercostal branch supplies skin
Motor only.
Limb buds arise from the lateral strip of the body wall
Supplied by lateral branches of anterior rami.
Posterior divisions supply extensor compartments
True. Posterior divisions of the plexuses supply extensor muscles and skin; anterior divisions supply flexors. (Last's)
The extensor compartment has the richer nerve supply
The flexor; the lowest root of each plexus goes wholly to flexors.
The cephalic vein marks the postaxial border of the upper limb
The preaxial border; basilic is postaxial.
Brachioradialis developed in the extensor compartment
Hence radial nerve supply.
The adult septum imprisons the ulnar nerve in the extensor compartment above the elbow
True. The ulnar nerve was a flexor-compartment nerve, but the medial intermuscular septum traps it behind, in the extensor compartment, above the elbow. (Last's)
The short head of biceps femoris developed in the flexor compartment
In the extensor; hence common peroneal supply.
The radial nerve lies in the extensor compartment just above the elbow
The septum places it in the flexor compartment.
There is no dermatomal overlap across axial lines
True. Adjacent dermatomes overlap, but dermatomes meeting at an axial line are discontinuous and do not, so test across axial lines. (Last's)
The upper limb anterior axial line starts near the sternal angle
Across the 2nd costal cartilage.
The posterior upper limb axial line ends at the wrist
At the deltoid insertion.
The root of the penis is S2
L1; the rest and scrotum S2/3.
C1 has no skin supply
True. C1 usually has no cutaneous branch; C2 supplies the back of the scalp. (Last's)
T10 supplies the umbilicus
True. T10 supplies the umbilicus; T4 the nipple and T8 the costal margin. (Last's)
C7 supplies the little finger
The middle finger; C8 the ring and little fingers.
T1 supplies the axilla
The medial elbow, not the axilla.
L4 supplies the medial malleolus
True. L4 supplies the medial leg and malleolus; L5 the dorsum and great toe; S1 the lateral foot. (Last's)
S3 supplies the sitting area of the buttock
True. S3 supplies the sitting area of the buttock and the posterior scrotum or labium. (Last's)
L5 supplies the lateral malleolus
S1 does.
S4 supplies the posterior thigh
Perianal.
Biceps jerk is C6
True. Biceps jerk C6, triceps C7, knee L3, ankle S1. (Last's)
Knee jerk is L3
True. The knee jerk is mediated mainly by L3 through the femoral nerve. (Last's)
Ankle jerk is L5
Abductor pollicis brevis is C6
Hip adduction is L2/3
True. Hip flexion, adduction and medial rotation are L2/3; extension, abduction and lateral rotation L4/5. (Last's)
Tibialis posterior is supplied by L4
With its inverting partner tibialis anterior.
Gluteus maximus is L4, 5, S1
Hip abduction is L2/3
The plantar response becomes flexor during the second year
True. An extensor plantar response is normal under one year; it becomes flexor in the second year. (Last's)
The anal and bulbocavernosus reflexes depend mainly on S3
True. The anal and bulbocavernosus reflexes depend on intact sacral segments, mainly S3. (Last's)
Abdominal reflexes are exaggerated in upper motor neuron lesions
They are absent.
In Beevor's sign the umbilicus moves downwards
Upwards.
The superior cervical ganglion represents C1-4
True. The upper four cervical ganglia fuse into the superior cervical ganglion, which gives grey rami to C1-4. (Last's)
Only T1-L2 give white rami
True. Only T1-L2 have lateral horn cells, so only they have white rami; every spinal nerve receives a grey ramus. (Last's)
Grey rami are preganglionic
Postganglionic.
Limb vessels receive sympathetics by fibres running long distances along the arteries
From adjacent peripheral nerves.
Sacral splanchnic nerves are sympathetic
True. Sacral splanchnic nerves are sympathetic branches of the sacral trunk to the pelvic plexus. (Last's)
Pelvic splanchnic nerves are parasympathetic
True. Pelvic splanchnic nerves are the S2-4 parasympathetic outflow; do not confuse the two. (Last's)
A proximal root lesion reduces sympathetic function in the limb
Sympathetics join distal to the roots, so peripheral lesions do.
Preganglionic fibres to the suprarenal synapse in the coeliac ganglion
They pass without synapse.
The embryo becomes a fetus after 8 weeks
True. The developing human is called an embryo for the first eight weeks and a fetus thereafter. (Last's)
Neural crest gives Schwann cells
And DRG, autonomic ganglia, suprarenal medulla.
Paraxial mesoderm gives the limb buds
The lateral plate does.
Intermediate mesoderm is unsegmented
The lateral plate is unsegmented.
The stapedial artery is a second arch remnant
True. The second arch artery disappears except for the stapedial artery. (Last's)
Stylopharyngeus is the third arch muscle
True. Stylopharyngeus is the only muscle of the third arch, supplied by IX. (Last's)
The mandible ossifies in Meckel's cartilage
In membrane; Meckel's remnants include the lingula.
The 4th arch forms the pulmonary arteries
The 6th does.
The third pouch forms the inferior parathyroid
And thymus.
The fourth pouch forms the superior parathyroid
True. The dorsal part of the fourth pouch forms the superior parathyroid. (Last's)
The second pouch forms the thymus
It forms the tonsillar crypts.
The fifth pouch forms the follicular thyroid cells
Ultimobranchial body and parafollicular cells.
A branchial fistula tracks between internal and external carotids
True. A branchial fistula runs from the tonsillar fossa between the internal and external carotids to the skin at the lower anterior border of SCM. (Last's)
An aberrant right subclavian makes the right laryngeal nerve non-recurrent
Incidence 1-2%.
The fistula opens at the posterior border of SCM
At the anterior lower border.
The chorda tympani is a post-trematic nerve
It is pretrematic.
The anterior fontanelle closes at about 18 months
True. The anterior fontanelle, between frontal and parietal bones, closes at about 18 months. (Last's)
The posterior fontanelle closes by the end of the first year
True. The posterior fontanelle, at the lambda, closes by the end of the first year. (Last's)
The mastoid is aerated at birth
From the beginning of the second year.
The geniculate ganglion is separated from middle fossa dura at birth
The tegmen is incomplete so it contacts the dura.
The squamous and tympanic parts ossify in membrane
True. The squamous and tympanic parts ossify in membrane; the petromastoid and styloid in cartilage. (Last's)
The foramen of Huschke is temporary
True. Growing flanges of the tympanic plate enclose a temporary gap, the foramen of Huschke, which normally closes in childhood. (Last's)
The facial nerve at birth is protected by the mastoid process
Unprotected, covered only by SCM.
The spinal cord ends at L1 at birth
